criteria.thresholds: Sexual Dysfunctions: >=6 months duration, ~75%-100% of occasions (DSM p.478). Paraphilias: Criterion A (erotic focus >=6 months) + Criterion B (Distress/Impairment or Harm to Nonconsenting Others) (DSM p.780). Pedophilic: Age >=16 and >=5 years older than child (DSM p.793). Voyeuristic: Age >=18 (DSM p.781).
subtypes: In a controlled environment / In full remission (DSM p.781)

epidemiology.prevalence: ED: 13%-21% (40-80y), 50%-75% (>70y) (DSM p.483); PE: 1%-3% strict 1-min IELT (DSM p.503); Pedophilic Disorder: <3% men (DSM p.794)
epidemiology.sex_ratio: Predominantly Male in Paraphilic Disorders (Voyeurism 2:1-3:1 M:F, Fetishism/Transvestic almost exclusively male) (DSM p.781, p.797, p.799)
epidemiology.onset_age_typical: Pedophilic: Puberty onset (DSM p.794); Masochism: Mean 19.3 years (DSM p.789); ED: Peaks >50 years (DSM p.483)
epidemiology.heritability: Premature Ejaculation linked to DAT and SERT gene polymorphisms (DSM p.503)
epidemiology.prognosis: Lifelong type persists without treatment; SSRI-induced sexual dysfunction remits in ~30% spontaneously by 6 months (DSM p.251, p.508)

etiology.genetic: DAT and SERT gene polymorphisms in Premature Ejaculation (DSM p.503); Low MAOA activity x childhood maltreatment (Dulcan p.208)
etiology.neurobiology: 5-HT2A/5-HT2C activation inhibits mesolimbic dopamine and spinal reflexes (StahlNeuro p.293); Paroxetine inhibits NOS (StahlNeuro p.293); D2 blockade in tuberoinfundibular path causes hyperprolactinemia & HPG suppression (StahlNeuro p.187); Paraphilias involve shift from Ventral Striatum (reward/dopamine) to Dorsal Striatum (habit/compulsivity) with OFC top-down failure (StahlNeuro p.538-540)
etiology.environmental: Childhood sexual/physical abuse, trauma, relationship distress, cultural/religious inhibitions (DSM p.477, p.782, Dulcan p.519)

first_line: Sensate Focus therapy for performance anxiety/ED (DSM p.484)
Pelvic floor CBT + graduated vaginal dilators for Genito-Pelvic Pain (DSM p.496-497)
CBT-SO (Cognitive restructuring & Relapse prevention) for Paraphilic Disorders (DSM p.794, Syllabus p.26)
Switch to Bupropion/Mirtazapine for SSRI-induced sexual dysfunction (StahlKids p.83, p.199, StahlNeuro p.308)
second_line: Augmentation with Buspirone (up to 60mg/day) or PDE-5i (Sildenafil) (StahlKids p.199, p.439)
GnRH Agonists (Leuprolide/Triptorelin) for severe Pedophilic/Paraphilic disorder (chemical castration) (StahlNeuro p.539, Dulcan p.575)
Anti-androgens (Cyproterone Acetate / Medroxyprogesterone) (StahlNeuro p.539, Dulcan p.575)
High-dose SSRIs off-label for compulsive paraphilic urges (StahlNeuro p.539)
key_side_effects: Osteoporosis & metabolic syndrome from GnRH agonists/Anti-androgens (Dulcan p.640-645)
Hyperprolactinemia, galactorrhea, gynecomastia from D2 blockers (StahlKids p.367)
treatment.monitoring: Bone mineral density (DEXA), plasma testosterone, prolactin, lipid profile, fasting glucose (DSM p.484, Dulcan p.640-645)

2.5x increase in perpetrator prosecution rate when objective CSA physical findings are present (Dulcan p.522)

high_yield: Criterion B is mandatory for Paraphilic Disorder: A paraphilia alone is not a mental disorder without distress, impairment, or harm to nonconsenting others (DSM p.780).
Paroxetine causes unique erectile dysfunction due to Nitric Oxide Synthase (NOS) inhibition in addition to 5-HT2A/2C activation (StahlNeuro p.293).
D2 blockade in the tuberoinfundibular pathway causes hyperprolactinemia, suppressing GnRH and gonadal steroids (StahlNeuro p.187, Dulcan p.824).
NPT during REM sleep is normal in psychogenic ED but impaired/absent in organic vascular ED (DSM p.484-485).
GnRH agonists (Leuprolide) induce chemical castration via pituitary GnRH receptor down-regulation for high-risk pedophilic offenders (StahlNeuro p.539, Dulcan p.575).
Low MAOA activity x childhood maltreatment doubles the risk of Conduct Disorder and aggressive behavior (Dulcan p.208).
